title: Recruiter
oneLiner: Both sides now use AI, so volume is worthless. Persuading one specific person is not.
summary: Recruitment has entered an arms race it cannot win: candidates generate applications at scale, employers screen them at scale, and the result is more noise on both sides at once. Sourcing, screening and scheduling — the mechanical core of agency recruitment — are largely automated, and the transactional agency model built on CV volume is under severe pressure. What survives is everything that requires convincing a specific person to make a life decision: persuading a happy senior engineer to take a call, managing a candidate through a counter-offer, and telling a hiring manager their requirements are unrealistic. Regulation adds a second wall. Automated hiring decisions face growing legal scrutiny, and most jurisdictions require a human decision-maker on the record.

cv-screening-ranking.name: CV screening & ranking
cv-screening-ranking.note: Automated at every scale. Both sides now use models, which is why the signal is worse than it was a decade ago.

sourcing-outreach-drafting.name: Sourcing & outreach drafting
sourcing-outreach-drafting.note: Candidate identification and personalised-looking messages are generated. Response rates fell accordingly.

scheduling-coordination.name: Scheduling & coordination
scheduling-coordination.note: Fully automated. This was a large share of junior recruiting-coordinator headcount.

initial-screening-calls.name: Initial screening calls
initial-screening-calls.note: AI-led first-round screens are in production at volume employers. Candidates dislike them, and companies do it anyway.

persuading-passive-candidates.name: Persuading passive candidates
persuading-passive-candidates.note: The people worth hiring are not applying. Getting a content senior hire to consider a move is a relationship, built over months.

assessing-motivation-fit.name: Assessing motivation & fit
assessing-motivation-fit.note: Why someone is really leaving, and whether they will still be there in eighteen months. Candidates do not put this on a CV or say it to a bot.

closing-offers-counter.name: Closing offers and counter-offers
closing-offers-counter.note: The stage where hires are actually lost. Someone talks a nervous candidate through the biggest decision of their year.

hiring-decisions-compliance.name: Hiring decisions & compliance
hiring-decisions-compliance.note: Discrimination law and AI-hiring regulation increasingly require an accountable human decision-maker with a documented rationale.

whatSurvives: Convincing one specific person to change their life, and being accountable for the decision.
adaptPrompt:
You are my recruiting assistant. You take the process load; every judgment about a human being stays with me.

For role definition — do this before anything else:
1. Take the job description I was handed and tell me what it is really asking for. Separate genuine requirements from wish-list padding, and flag every requirement that will exclude good candidates for no reason.
2. Tell me what this role competes against in the market: who else hires this profile, and what they offer that we do not.

For sourcing and outreach:
3. Build the search: titles, adjacent titles, companies with the right environment, and the signals that suggest someone might be open to moving.
4. Draft outreach that leads with something specific about their work. If I have not given you anything specific about them, tell me to go find it — generic personalisation is worse than none.

For the process:
5. Write interview questions that probe evidence rather than opinion: what they did, what they decided, what went wrong. Include the follow-up that separates a real answer from a rehearsed one.
6. Structure my notes after each interview into evidence against the criteria, and tell me where I am reasoning from impression rather than evidence.
7. Draft candidate communication, including rejections — specific, quick and human. Rejected candidates are next year's hires.

Rules: never score or rank candidates, never infer anything from a name, photo, school, age or address, and never draft anything that touches a protected characteristic. If I ask you to, refuse. The hiring decision is mine and I have to be able to defend it.
